analysis.investment_thesis: Supertech EV is a 2022-incorporated micro-cap (INR 54 Cr m-cap) EV 2W/e-rickshaw player with near-zero profitability (ROE 0.47%) and no track record. The EV tailwind is real, but this company has no scale, no moat, and no proof of execution to justify betting on it.
key_strengths: EV 2W/e-rickshaw sector has genuine structural tailwinds from FAME/PLI and rising adoption
Promoter holding healthy at 69.31% — skin in the game
Headline P/E of 8.21x looks optically cheap
key_risks: ROE of 0.47% is effectively broken — business is not earning its cost of capital
3-year-old company with no proven execution against Ola, TVS, Bajaj, Ather, Hero
Micro-cap INR 54 Cr size — liquidity, governance, and scale-up risk very high
red_flags: ROE below 1% despite positive P/E suggests razor-thin earnings base — any slip turns loss-making
Hyper-competitive EV 2W space dominated by well-capitalized incumbents
Zero DII holding — no institutional validation of the story
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Indian EV 2-wheeler and e-rickshaw opportunity is one I would back enthusiastically — it rides consumption, urbanization, and policy tailwinds. But the sector will be won by players with capital, distribution, and technology depth: Ola Electric, TVS, Bajaj, Ather, Hero Vida. Supertech EV, incorporated only in 2022 with a market cap of just INR 54 Cr and ROE of 0.47%, is a sub-scale participant in a capital-intensive, margin-thin game. The 8.21x P/E is meaningless when the "E" is so tiny that it's essentially noise — a single bad quarter flips this to loss-making.

Promoter holding at 69.31% is the one genuine positive, but without a long track record I cannot assess promoter quality — and in India, that is the single most important variable. I invest in businesses I can hold for 5-15 years with conviction; nothing in this data gives me that conviction. Much better to play the EV theme through proven promoters (Bajaj, TVS) or, if chasing the pure-play, wait for scale and unit economics to be demonstrated. Avoid.
